# Every permission the release APK may ask for, as Exodus's scanner reads it from the merged manifest.
# exodus-scan.sh fails a build whose APK asks for anything not listed here, or no longer asks for
# something that is: a permission can't arrive (or leave) unnoticed through a library's manifest.
# A permission the app declares itself is also explained to the user in the app.

# Declared by the app (AndroidManifest.xml) and explained in the app where it is asked for.
# The Scan screen's permission page, before Android's prompt (#10):
android.permission.CAMERA
# Product lookup in Open Food Facts (#9, docs/adr/0001): granted at install, so the scan sheet asks before
# the first lookup and the README explains it.
android.permission.INTERNET
# The daily expiry digest (#27): asked for in Pantry settings when an expiration alert is turned on
# (Android 13 and later), and explained under the alerts there.
android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS
# The digest's alarm, set again after a restart (Android clears alarms). Install-time; Pantry settings say
# the digest goes out once a day. An inexact alarm, so no SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM, and no WorkManager, which
# would add WAKE_LOCK, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE and FOREGROUND_SERVICE.
android.permission.RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED

# Merged in from libraries. Install-time; the user is never asked for it.
# androidx.core, which protects the app's own unexported receivers with it:
io.cosgriff.pantry.DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION
